html:
The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was the peace signed on 3 March 1918 at Brest, in today's Belarus, between Soviet Russia and Germany and its allies, ending Russia's part in World War I.

Lenin insisted on peace at almost any price to save the revolution. Russia gave up Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland, Belarus and Ukraine, about a third of its population and much of its industry and farmland. Germany planned to rule these lands through puppet states. The treaty was cancelled after Germany's defeat in November 1918, but it opened the way for the Belarusian People's Republic, the Ukrainian state and the independent Baltic states and Poland.
